newsitem.title: INDIA: India regional party considers quitting coalition.
newsitem.headline: India regional party considers quitting coalition.

text.p: India's regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party is considering whether to pull out of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's ruling United Front coalition, the United News of India (UNI) said on Monday.

But the party, to which Industry Minister Murasoli Maran belongs, plans to continue support from outside to the government, the news agency quoted party president Muthuvel Karunandhi as saying in the southern city of Madras.
The party from the southern state of Tamil Nadu said it was unwilling to work with other unnamed members of the government.

"The DMK was not willing to go along with parties which were functioning with minimal plans and persons trying to fulfil their personal ambitions," Karunanidhi was quoted as saying by Press Trust of India, the country's other major news agency.

There was no immediate threat to Gujral's government. The DMK has 20 lawmakers in the 545-member lower house of parliament, in which the United Front has an overall strength of 178. The coalition gets make-or-break support from the Congress party, which has 140 members.

"The DMK is not willing to go along with the personal whims of some leaders and the private minimum programmes of certain parties," the regional party's president, Muthuvel Karunanidhi, said in a statement in Madras, capital of the state of Tamil Nadu.
"Until the situation improves, the DMK is planning to stay out of the ministry and support the government from outside," Karunanidhi, who is also the state's chief minister said in the statement.

The statement did not give details, but party politicians said it could have been directed at the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), which has taken a hardline against a petroleum price hike and against admitting a breakaway political group into the coalition.
